rationale: This is a straight leg-swap between two archived signals — the che/market value leg from "Operating-Quality Backed Cash Discount"/"Liability-Maturity Adjusted Cash Discount" combined with the exact gross-profit-over-lct quality leg from "Gross-Profit Claim Covered Cashflow Yield" — so it is a cosmetic recombination rather than a substantively new mechanism.

The economics are coherent (cheap cash is only credible if residual post-dividend cash flow covers creditor claims), but the construction is again a two-way recombination of archived pieces — the (oancf−dvc)/liabilities leg from "After-Payout Liability Cover Yield" with the cash-to-market value leg — differing only by lct→lt, which is unlikely to generate independent evidence.

The level of the short-term liability share as a conditioner on cash-flow yield is distinct from the archived change-in-lct/lt trap signal and the expression matches the stated positive-sign hypothesis, though lct/lt is heavily industry- and business-model-driven and the value leg is a standard cash-flow-to-price anomaly, so the incremental content is modest.

Internally consistent (high payout yield × rising liabilities loads high, predicted negative) and not a direct archive rediscovery, but the liability-growth leg is close to the well-documented net debt issuance/asset growth anomaly, and dvc/market has a large mass of tied zeros for non-payers that will blunt the RANK leg.

This is essentially the archived "Net-Current-Asset EBITDA Yield" with ni substituted for ebitda — a numerator swap on an already-tested signal whose FMB slope came out significantly opposite to the expected sign, so it re-tests a known contradiction rather than diagnosing it.

It stacks the archived EBITDA/EV multiple with two previously tested quality legs whose components share the same lct scaling, making the SUMRANK largely redundant and the whole construct an incremental variant of "Cash-Covered EBITDA Enterprise Value" and "Liability-Maturity Adjusted Cash Discount".
